newsitem.title: JAPAN: FOCUS-Hokkaido Takushoku, Barclays to form alliance.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Hokkaido Takushoku, Barclays to form alliance.

text.p: Troubled Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd said on Monday it will work out a cooperative arrangement with Britain's Barclays Bank, giving the Japanese bank's restructuring scheme the finishing touch.

The two banks said they will begin discussions aimed at working together in several areas, including the development of new financial products and the securitisation of housing loans and other assets held by Hokkaido Takushoku.
But a Hokkaido Takushoku executive told reporters that neither bank had any intention of taking a stake in the other.
Andrew Simmonds, chief executive of Barclays group in Japan, told reporters that Barclays wants to help Hokkaido Takushoku's customers access overseas capital markets.
He said that the agreement to explore areas of cooperation is non-exclusive, although the British bank had no plans for any tie-ups with other Japanese partners.
In April, Hokkaido Takushoku, Japan's 10th-largest commercial bank, announced that it would merge with the smaller regional bank Hokkaido Bank Ltd in April 1998 to restart as Shin-Hokkaido Bank.
The bank had long been considered the most troubled of Japan's major city banks, burdened with bad assets after Japan's bubble of inflated land and share prices burst in the early 1990s.
Hokkaido Takushoku said at the time it announced the merger that it would withdraw from overseas operations by March 1998.

This is the second major business alliance unveiled between a troubled Japanese bank and a foreign bank this year, following a similar announcement by Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) and Bankers Trust New York Corp.
Heavily indebted NCB, another victim of the asset bubble, announced a radical restructuring plan on the same day that Hokkaido Takushoku and Hokkaido Bank unveiled their merger.
NCB's plan included the termination of its overseas operations, the sale of prime real estate and the floating of new shares to try to rebuild its capital base.
Later in April, NCB and Bankers Trust signed a memorandum of understanding concerning business collaboration in securitisation operations, overseas financial business and support services.
They said they would consider a limited amount of mutual capital participation after NCB completes its capital restructuring.
